source: A real attached session (`01a1f574-af12-…`, cwd /private/tmp/unbien-capture) recorded by the web client itself: loaded with `?capture=1`, which tees every inbound envelope to `window.__unbienFrames`, then `__unbienDump("022-raw")`. `raw.jsonl` is that dump — UNSCRUBBED, not committed. `capture.py` turns it into the two committed inputs.
extensionVersion: @geohar/un-bien 0.25.15 (the build installed in this pi). The repo's extension source is at 0.25.11; see vocab.md, 'Which build produced this'.
scrub: capture.py, field-aware — the same rules 021 worked out and records in full: message content is length-preserving `░` filler at any length (row identity is a hash of message content, so a marker there breaks the pair), while tool-RESULT prose, base64 `data`, `partialResult` and long `details.*` values become `«length»` markers, and shape (`type`, `role`, `mimeType`, `toolCallId`, ids, timestamps, stopReasons, usage) is never touched.
description: The compaction fixture nobody had: a session whose log was ALREADY COMPACTED before the viewer attached, with the compaction entry ON the active path. A human drove a session, compacted it (85 963 tokens before, `firstKeptEntryId` 59041a36), and only THEN did this client attach — so the compaction arrived purely as a durable entry, never as a live `compaction_end` frame. The compaction entry `d80b313f…` was the leaf of the attach walk, and every later turn is its child, so the backwalk runs straight through it. The client then watched four turns (949 streamed deltas, four tool calls) and a final walk of 45 entries with leaf beacon `a19bf1e2`, which is also what a cold arrival gets.
pairing: Held to the same golden in both runners, cold rows contained in the watched rows with identical fields, and the off-path row count pinned for the scenarios that branch (021: 37). This session did NOT branch, which is the point — 021's compaction ended up off the active path, so nothing before this fixture had ever proved a viewer could see a compaction it did not watch.
trims: One reduction: WALK COLLAPSE, 30 walk runs down to the first and the final (28 dropped; the final walk carries all 45 entries). Deltas are NOT trimmed here — four turns and 949 frames is 1 MB total, and every turn in this session is live traffic worth keeping.
note: What this fixture earned, on the first fold: BOTH implementations render the cold compaction correctly (a `compaction` row, text built from `tokensBefore`, keyed by the pi entry id `d80b313f…`), and the pair holds — the watched run gets the same row from the same entry, because it never saw a live marker either. But probing the OTHER half — a compaction that streams live and later arrives in a walk — found a defect in both folds, which is why 022 also compacted nothing live (`/compact` refused: the log had just been compacted, too little to fold). A live marker is keyed on the bare sequence number and an entry-born marker on the entry id, and nothing matches one to the other, so the watched transcript gets TWO 'Context compacted' rows for one compaction. `web-client/test/compaction-durability.test.ts` and the reference's `SessionStateTests` case pin the fix (both: one row, re-keyed from the bare sequence number to the entry id). The web test assembles the pair from two real shapes — 022's on-path entry, 021's live `compaction_end` shape — because no capture yet shows a compaction that was BOTH watched live and later walked on-path; that capture is the obvious next one.; 022 itself cannot show the duplicate, because its compaction was cold.
